summary: Weekly coaching 1-1 between Chris Klevan (sales manager) and Andrew Musial (closer). Two topics. First, the open-wallet money play: Chris delivers the exact scripted framing he wants Andrew using — that there are no set payment plans, everything is custom, Trevor does not want anyone choosing between rent and training, followed by a permission question — and coaches Andrew to soften his tonality and stay neutral rather than treating the prospect as a logic problem. Second, July projections. Chris walks Andrew through his actual funnel numbers, works up a 154-to-100 live-call model at a 65% show rate and a 30% close rate, lands on $180K revenue and $126K cash collected, and pushes him to project $100K. Andrew resists on fear of being held to the number; Chris reframes projections as an accountability mechanism and Andrew commits.
notable: Stated payment-plan policy, from the manager, verbatim: "we don't really have any set payment plans. Everything we do is totally custom." Chris explains the framing is deliberately loose so reps can avoid being pinned to specific options — "they're not gonna ask you, well, what payment options do you have? You would just be like, well, I don't know. It really depends." This is the reference point against which payment-plan behaviour on live calls should be checked.

Chris coaches nationality-based lead screening: he tells Andrew to report prospects from Sri Lanka and the Middle East so they can be marked DQ, and to escalate them immediately by name of country. This is a manager instructing a rep to filter leads by national origin.

Baseline performance data for Andrew, June: 126 slots available, 80 booked, 45 live calls, 14 closes including a deposit, about a 30% close rate, 56.25% slot-to-show against a 64-65% team average. Richard is cited at 72% slot-to-show.
Commercial modelling assumption stated on the record: about 70% of contract value is collected upfront on average.

Andrew self-identifies his weakness as the finance conversation specifically — "I don't think I have issues with discovery anymore... I think just dialing in the finances. I think this is the thing." On a prospect call recorded within hours of this 1-1 he abandoned the money conversation entirely and downsold.
Andrew admits he had not done the assigned practice: "I haven't had time to actually practice what we started yesterday" and "No, I didn't. Sorry" when asked about the video sent to him.
